name: zld (faster fork of Apple ld64)
baseline: Apple's default macOS linker called through cc: ld-prime with Xcode 15 or later, ld64 when zld was current
verdict_reason: zld claimed links at least 40% faster than ld64, but it was archived in February 2023 and its author points to lld instead. Apple replaced ld64 with ld-prime in Xcode 15, and Chromium now measures ld-prime as faster than lld, so the baseline zld beat is gone.
tier_reason: The only number in text is a floor ('at least 40% faster'); the results themselves are an SVG chart.
claimed_speedup: Linking at least 40% faster than Apple's linker (README text; full results in a chart)
workload: Not stated in text; the README says zld is meant for debug builds, and the results are in an SVG chart
platforms: macOS; required a full Xcode install
install: Archived; old prebuilt binaries on the GitHub releases page
one_liner: Archived fork of Apple's old ld64 that claimed links at least 40% faster; Xcode 15's ld-prime replaced the linker it improved on.
how_it_is_fast: zld forked the last open-source release of Apple's ld64 and changed its hashing code for speed, keeping output otherwise byte-for-byte identical. It also kept caches between runs, so repeat links were faster than the first.
skip_it_when: Any build on Xcode 15 or later, where the default ld-prime replaced the ld64 baseline
Projects that need a maintained linker
caveats: Numbers are a chart image plus a 'not at least 40% faster' floor in text
Measured against ld64, which is no longer the default
tradeoffs: Archived and tied to an old ld64 version; may break with newer Xcode

evidence.quote: ## NOTE: zld is now archived, consider using lld instead.
## A faster version of Apple's linker
Feel free to file an issue if you find that linking is not at least 40% faster for your case
Without a few optimizations around hashing, it would produce byte-for-byte the same executables as the open-source one.
Recent benchmarks show that Apple's new linker (ld-prime) is faster than LLD for local macOS development
